# aeneid-026 (IV.206–304) — reviewer's record

Two passes: (1) every grammatical label against its form and line; (2) Latin to `l` word by word, `l`/`i`
agreement, line division of `l` against `t`, remembered English in `i`, speech marks. Scansion: every line was
read against the scanner output by hand (all 99 lines, not only the flagged ones). `units.json` is now the
authority; `draft.py` was regenerated from it so the two agree. `t`, `ln`, `p`, `v` are untouched (checked by
script against the pre-review file; the tiling is unchanged). No modern translation was consulted.

Counts: units/notes **major 3, medium 18, low 9**; scansion **major 3, medium 5, low 1**.
Overall **major 6, medium 23, low 10**.

## Speech marks (checked, no change needed)
“ opens unit 0 (206), unit 6 (223 — Jupiter), unit 28 (265 — Mercury, after `Continuo invadit:`).
” closes unit 3 (218), unit 12 (237), unit 32 (276). `t` carries Greenough's `debentur. ”` (space, then mark,
then `Tali` on the next unit); left exactly as printed. `l` and `i` carry the same marks on the same units.

## Units — major
- **Unit 26 (261–264) `l`, `n`.** `l` read “which, rich gifts, Dido” — `dives` is Dido's, not the gifts' — and put
  `ensis` on the line of `atque illi stellatus iaspide fulva` (it belongs to 262). Rewritten with the correct
  line division and `dives` kept with Dido. The note called `quae` the cloak with `munera` a predicate noun and
  said nothing of the other parse; it now says `quae` is both fem. sg. (→ `laena`) and neut. pl. (→ `munera`),
  with the same sense either way (the drafter's doubt at 263).
- **Unit 18 (245) `n`.** “`fretus`, the perfect participle of the deponent `fretus sum`” is false: `fretus` is an
  adjective governing the ablative. Fixed.
- **Unit 6 (223–226) `n`.** The explanation of `labere`/`adloquere` (“stem `labe-`, `adloque-`”) was garbled, and
  `Dardanium ducem` was said to be “held to the head of the next line” (it stands at the head of 224; its verb
  `adloquere` stands at the head of 226). Both corrected.

## Units — medium
- **0 (206–210) `l`:** `te` after `an` was missing (`an te … horremus`, “shudder at you”), and `pictis` was
  moved to the wrong line (`pictis`/`toris` straddle 206/207). Rewritten.
- **3 (217–218) `l`:** `munera` was dropped from the 217 line; redivided.
- **4 (219–221) `l`, `n`:** `regia` (221) sat on the 220 line; `n` claimed `moenia regia` “framed around” the
  verb, which it is not. Fixed.
- **7 (227–228) `l`, `n`:** `illum` omitted from `l`; `n` said `vindicat` “looks back over two escapes”
  (unverifiable). Now: `non` carried over from the first clause is stated openly as a requirement of the sense
  (the Latin repeats no negative); `Graium` = `Graiorum` with `armis` (doubt at 228); `bis` counts two rescues
  without naming them. The reading is kept.
- **8 (229–231) `n`:** `Italiam` is not “the last word of its line” (it opens 230). `proderet` “bring into the
  world” changed to “hand down, transmit” to agree with `i`.
- **9 (232–234) `l`, `i`:** `ipse` was rendered “on his own account” without being a word-for-word match; `i` had
  a future (“will not take”) for the present `molitur`. Fixed (same for 273 in unit 32).
- **12 (237) `n`, `l`:** `hic nostri nuntius esto` is ambiguous (`nuntius` = “message” or “messenger”, `hic` =
  `haec summa` or Mercury). Note now says so and states which reading we follow. `l` now keeps `nostri`.
- **15 (239–241) `n`:** `talaria` was called “the subject-antecedent” of `quae … portant`; it is the object of
  `nectit` and the antecedent.
- **17 (242–244) `n`, `l`:** the `resignat` doubt (244). Note rewritten to state the debate honestly: basic sense
  “unseal, open”; second sense “cancel, annul”; `morte` as “by/from death”; so the clause can be read as
  “opens eyes death had sealed”, “cancels death for the eyes”, or “seals the eyes in death”. We keep “unseals”;
  `i` unchanged. “Asyndetic” removed (there is an `-que`). `l` re-ordered to follow the Latin.
- **19 (246–249) `l`:** `piniferum caput` (249) was on the 248 line; redivided.
- **20 (250) `n`:** `umeros` can go with `tegit` or with `infusa` (Greek-style accusative); both stated.
- **24 (256–258) `i`:** “the child of Cyllene” suggests a nymph Cyllene; `Cyllenia proles` is “the Cyllenian
  offspring”. Fixed.
- **28 (265–267) `l`:** `you` (subject of `exstruis`) was on the 266 line; redivided.
- **32 (272–276) `l`, `i`:** `respice` (275) sat on the 274 line; the bracketed 273 now parallels 233; `i` had
  “will not take” for `moliris` and two seemingly separate persons (“Ascanius … Iulus”); now one boy.
- **42 (291–294) `l`, `n`:** `tempora` (294) sat on the 293 line; `quis rebus` called a “dative of interest”
  (the construction is open between dative and ablative; the note now says so); “(`sint`)” → “(`sint`, `sit`)”.
- **43 (294–295) `n`:** the note called `imperio` ablative with `laeti` and dative with `parent` at once; now says
  it can do either and says which version takes which.
- **46 (297) `n`:** “used of words at 114” cites a line not in this part and unverifiable; removed.
- **48 (300–303) `l`, `n`:** `stimulant` (302) was on the 303 line; redivided. `trieterica` (doubt at 303): note
  now says Greek “every third year” counting both ends = every other year, the literal `l` says “triennial”,
  `i` gives the real interval.

## Units — low
- 1: `i` “strayed into” → “wandered in” (`errans in finibus`); `n` “Dido bought her land” hedged (“the story is”).
- 2: `n` “Dido herself is the plunder” → Dido and her kingdom.
- 3: `i` “a hollow report of your power” → “a hollow rumour” (nothing in the Latin for “of your power”).
- 6: `l` “come” → “come on”; `i` rephrased (close to a standard English opening).
- 12: `i` rephrased (echo risk).
- 14: `n` “frames the sentence” removed.
- 16: `n` “caduceus in the later tradition” → “usually called the caduceus”.
- 18, 20, 21, 33, 45: `i` adjusted for fidelity (`tranat` kept as swimming; `infusa` participle; `riget` beard; `ex oculis` “from
  before his eyes” for the undefined “their eyes”; `quis fallere possit amantem` rephrased).
- 25: `n` “still stand where the city is rising” (not in the Latin) → “huts or cottages, a word of Punic origin”.
- 30: `n` “as messengers in epic do” → “often do”.
- 8: `i` aligned with `n` (see above).

## Scansion (hand-scanned; added to `scan-fixes.json`)
Every line was scanned by hand against the scanner's printout. Lines whose scanner fit was correct and which are
not in the file: every line except the nine below (including 4.213 `cuique … conubia`, cost 1.5:
the fit has the right quantities; 4.230 `Teucri`: diphthong, one syllable, correct; 4.302 `Thyias`: dissyllabic by
synizesis, the only fit, correct; 4.216 `mitra` needs long `mī` — the only fit; 4.215 `semiviro` needs long `sē` —
the only fit). Added (9):

| line | problem | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 4.214 | `Aenean` read with synizesis, `dominum` made long-long (cost 1.5) | Ae-nē-an, long `an` before `in` (as 1.631) |
| 4.235 | `i-ni` made long-long to elide `spe` (cost 0.0) | hiatus after `spe`, natural quantities — **UNCONFIRMED** |
| 4.259 | `primum` short, `tetigit` long-long (cost 0.0) | prī-, ā-lā-tis, tĕ-tĭ-git, mā-gā- |
| 4.260 | `Ae-` split (cost 1.2) | Ae-nē-an |
| 4.274 | scanner took `Iuli` as consonantal (cost 2.0, flagged) | Ĭūlī trisyllabic, as 1.267/1.556/aeneid-006,008,015 |
| 4.279 | `Ae-` split, `vero` unelided (cost 1.2) | Ae-nē-ās; obmūtuit long ū |
| 4.293 | `temptaturum` short-short, `aditus` long-long (cost 0.8) | tempt-ā-tū-rum, ă-dĭ-tūs |
| 4.296 | `regina` short-short (cost 0.0; as 4.1) | rē-gī-na |
| 4.304 | `Ae-` split (cost 1.2) | Ae-nē-an, `tandem his` elision |

All nine pass the validator's six-foot pattern test and the build's word-match test (checked with a scratch
script, not the build).

## Refused / left as drafted
- 228 `Graium` and the carried-over `non`: reading kept (see unit 7); stated in the note.
- 273 bracketed line: kept in `t`, `l`, `i`; the note already says Greenough brackets it and why. No change.
- 263 `dives quae munera Dido`: `i` kept (“a gift that rich Dido had made”); note and `l` fixed.
- 244 `resignat`: `i` and the “unseal” reading kept; note made honest.
- 303 `trieterica`: `l` “triennial” kept as the literal layer.
- The Latin Library variants at 221, 257, 276: the drafter notes them although they change little (the convention
  says to note only variants that change the sense). Harmless; left.
- 4.213, 4.215, 4.216, 4.230, 4.302 scansions: no fix, reasons above.
- The note on unit 0 that Iarbas is a son of Jupiter Hammon (stated in IV.198–199, not in this part): left; it
  cannot be checked inside this part.
- The `i` wording could not be compared with any English version (none opened); only phrasing that looked
  formulaic was rephrased (units 6, 12, 21, 45).

## For QUESTIONS.md
1. 4.235 `spe inimica`: hiatus (my reading) versus elision with long `i-ni` (scanner). Neither checked
   against an edition.
2. 4.216 `mitra` (long `mī`) and 4.215 `semiviro` (long `sē`): forced by the metre, quantities unconfirmed.
3. 4.274 `Iuli`: now trisyllabic (house practice); the scanner preferred the consonantal reading.
4. 4.244 `resignat`, 4.237 `nuntius`, 4.263 `quae`: the notes now state the open readings; the owner may prefer a
   different rendering in `i`.
5. 4.276 closing mark printed by Greenough after the full stop with a space (`debentur. ”Tali`): kept in `t`.
